active_conjecture.summary: Can normalized implicit-copy operations implement useful collective binary detection or symmetry-breaking identification? Carrier extraction does not establish this. An older local systematic-core proof claim was also withdrawn without refuting the independent global BABA argument.

execution_model: Research generation and experiments run interactively during active Codex sessions. A GitHub workflow validates pushed snapshots, and a scheduled backup can commit only validation-passing changes; neither mechanism performs autonomous quantum-algorithm research between sessions.

milestones.detail: Fifty-four exact character-ratio inequalities prove lambda_min(F)>=(71/825)n^-5 and polynomial inverse-square-root filters for two involution families.

milestones.detail: Its exact probability is d_W^3 d_xi Tr(F)/(n!)^3, at most (25/3)n^9/(n!)^3; postselection and generic amplification are superpolynomial.
milestones.title: Natural access kills the fixed stable branch

milestones.detail: For fixed K, total weak-Fourier mass is at most 2 P_K n^(2K)/n!. Uniform adaptation to typical high-dimensional partitions is now mandatory.
milestones.title: Every fixed bounded-tail route is cut

milestones.detail: TC2/TT1 and its disjoint extension are exactly degenerate at n=8. Exact parameterized fourth moments instead prove TT1+c*TC1 has simple spectrum for every c!=0 on 6 n=8 targets of multiplicity at most four, including both known collisions. Exact quotient transfer at c=1 extends this to 20/20 targets through multiplicity 17. Degree-28 transfer and class-Fourier contraction extend fixed-c1 separation to 27/27 n=9 targets. All-n, gap, transform, and decoder questions remain separate; typical complete-label inverse-polynomial gaps are obstructed.
milestones.title: An independent third generator repairs the known finite collisions

overview: The current target is a useful measurement, not complete labels for every multiplicity. Spectral packing obstructs fixed-count normalized complete labels with inverse-polynomial gaps. Two QFTs instead extract a known subgroup carrier with an implicit copy code. Fixed-reference invariant identification is limited. Independent carrier discard also loses binary information; coherent retention does not itself supply a useful effect. Numerical checks are not formal proofs.

tracks.evidence: The all-target census evaluated millions of legal targets; the remaining question is a source-conditioned reduced-basis theorem, not another target sweep.

tracks.summary: Two-QFT restriction preserves normalization and supports logical orbit averages without decoding a copy basis. Independent carrier discard loses the detection signal. A joint quantum label front end plus classical processing reproduces the tested small-group binary gains. Clean subset labels and exact two-copy scoring are available; the growing-copy binary measurement remains missing. No useful detector or access to the unknown centralizer is supplied.
